lines: Splits one polyphonic keyboard stream into two note ranges, each with its own five output jacks and each switchable between passing its channels through and reducing them to one monophonic voice
Sets the note at and above which an incoming note goes to Zone B, everything below it going to Zone A; -4V to 4V, so eight octaves either side of C4
Arms the module to take its split point from the next note played at the V/Oct input; that note is held back from both zones, and clicking again cancels without a note being played
Switches Zone A to a single monophonic voice whose gate stays high across overlapping notes and drops only when the zone empties; unlit, the zone's channels pass through at their own channel numbers
Switches Zone B to a single monophonic voice whose gate stays high across overlapping notes and drops only when the zone empties; unlit, the zone's channels pass through at their own channel numbers
The polyphonic pitch cable from a MIDI-CV module at 1V per octave; the number of channels on this cable is how many the module reads
The polyphonic gate cable; a channel counts as held while it is at 1V or more
The polyphonic velocity cable, copied to whichever zone each channel falls in
The polyphonic aftertouch cable, copied to whichever zone each channel falls in
The polyphonic retrigger cable; an edge here is what sorts a channel into its zone, and without one a channel is sorted the first time it is found with its gate high
Zone A's pitch at 1V per octave: one channel per input channel in polyphonic mode, or a single channel carrying the priority note in monophonic mode
Zone A's gate: the input gate for the channels in this zone and 0V for the others in polyphonic mode, or one channel at 10V while any note in the zone is held in monophonic mode
Zone A's velocity: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's velocity on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone A's aftertouch: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's aftertouch on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone A's retrigger: the input retrigger for channels in this zone in polyphonic mode, or a 1ms pulse in monophonic mode fired only for a genuinely new key press
Zone B's pitch at 1V per octave: one channel per input channel in polyphonic mode, or a single channel carrying the priority note in monophonic mode
Zone B's gate: the input gate for the channels in this zone and 0V for the others in polyphonic mode, or one channel at 10V while any note in the zone is held in monophonic mode
Zone B's velocity: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's velocity on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone B's aftertouch: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's aftertouch on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone B's retrigger: the input retrigger for channels in this zone in polyphonic mode, or a 1ms pulse in monophonic mode fired only for a genuinely new key press
Menu — Monophonic priority (Zone A): Last note, Highest note, Lowest note — chooses which of the overlapping held notes Zone A plays while it is monophonic
Menu — Monophonic priority (Zone B): Last note, Highest note, Lowest note — chooses which of the overlapping held notes Zone B plays while it is monophonic
Note — the reading at the top shows the split note and its frequency, and right-clicking it opens a field where a note name such as C4 or F#3 can be typed in place of turning the knob
Note — while Learn is armed every output is set to no channels at all, so nothing plays until the split note has been taken
Note — feeding one zone's five outputs into a second Zones module splits that range again, which is how three or more zones are built from one keyboard
Note — in polyphonic mode the pitch, velocity and aftertouch outputs hold their last value on a channel that has left the zone; only the gate and retrigger drop at once
Note — only the first sixteen channels of the input cables are read

Zones.notes: The maker's README names the two priority menu items 'Zone A priority (when monophonic)' and 'Zone B priority (when monophonic)'; the code creates them as 'Monophonic priority (Zone A)' and '(Zone B)' (src/Zones.cpp:602-611), which is what the menu prints. The split test is pitch greater than or equal to the threshold for Zone B, so the split note itself belongs to Zone B. The velocity and aftertouch ports are given no range because nothing in the module scales or clamps them; they are passed through as they arrive. The Aluminium theme submenu is on every module of this plugin and is left out of the lines.

lines: Sixteen gate outputs, one per learned note: each output goes high while the note learned into its cell is held on the incoming polyphonic pitch and gate pair
Turns that cell's output into a toggle, switching on and off on each fresh press of its note in place of following the held note; learning or clearing that cell turns this back off
The polyphonic pitch cable the cells are matched against, and the cable that notes are learned from; it usually comes from a MIDI-CV module or from a Zones output
The polyphonic gate cable; a channel counts as held at 1V or more, and a rising edge here is what an armed cell captures as its note
10V while the note learned into that cell is held on any channel of the input, or while that cell is toggled on in latch mode, and 0V otherwise, including for a cell with no note
Menu — Add an expander — places a PadX immediately to the right of this module, or to the right of the last expander already chained there
Menu — Clear unpatched cells — clears the note from every cell whose own gate output has no cable in it, leaving the patched cells alone
Menu — Invert latches — turns latch on for every cell that had it off, and off for every cell that had it on
Menu — Factory presets — on Rack's own Preset submenu: ready-made cell mappings, chromatic and white-key or black-key runs, the stock pad maps for two controllers, and Unmapped for a clean slate
Note — a cell is learned by clicking it and playing the note on the incoming cable, or by clicking it and typing a letter from A to G, a # for a sharp and a digit for the octave, then Enter
Note — control-click, or command-click on a Mac, arms a cell for sequential learning, so each note captured arms the next cell and a whole row of pads can be mapped in one pass
Note — Escape, or clicking the armed cell again, cancels a learn and leaves that cell as it was; Backspace or Delete clears the cell to two dashes and its output then stays at 0V
Note — the same note is never mapped twice: learning a note into one cell clears it from whichever other cell held it
Note — a module fresh from the browser comes up with a chromatic run, C2 in the first cell up to D sharp 3 in the sixteenth, meant as something to learn over
Note — a cell shows a short line above its note name while that note is held on the input, and a line below while its own output is high; with latch on for that cell, the two can differ
Note — the first output is the top cell of the display's left column and the sixteenth is the bottom of its right column, running down each column in turn
Note — the sixteen cells are drawn inside one display widget rather than as separate controls, so no help line can be reached by clicking a cell
Note — only the first sixteen channels of the input cables are read

Pads.notes: Every one of the sixteen gate outputs is written by the same two lines (src/Pads.cpp:170-171), so one props entry covers them all. Where two channels carry the same note, the later channel is the one an expander follows (src/Pads.cpp:147). Latch toggles on the rising edge of the note match, not on the raw gate, so a latched cell does not retrigger while the note is held. The expander message carries the raw note match rather than the latched state, so a PadX on a velocity lane follows the physical note even where the gate output is latched on.

lines: Pads expander: it splits one polyphonic lane, such as velocity or aftertouch, into sixteen mono outputs, one per note Pads has learned; it goes immediately to the right of Pads or of another PadX
The polyphonic cable to split up, usually the velocity, aftertouch or retrigger output of whatever feeds Pads its pitch and gate
Whatever this lane currently carries for the note learned into the matching cell of Pads, or 0V while that cell has no note, its note is not held, or this cable has too few channels to reach it
Note — the field on the panel is a label to click and type into; it renames the tooltips on this module's jacks and changes nothing about the signal
Note — the label fills itself in from the first cable patched in while it is empty, taking eight characters of the source jack's name, and empties again when that cable is pulled out
Note — the lamp is yellow while nothing is patched into the lane, red while this cable has a different channel count from the pitch and gate cable feeding Pads, and green when the two match
Note — with no Pads to the left, directly or through other expanders, every output stays at 0V
Note — several of these can be chained, one per lane, in any order; each passes the note mapping on to the next
Note — a label typed in by hand is never cleared automatically; only one that filled itself in from a cable is

PadX.notes: No family is given to these ports: the module passes on whatever lane is patched into it, and the maker's own manual says the module does not care which lane that is. All sixteen outputs are written by the same three lines (src/PadX.cpp:128-132), so one props entry covers them. A channel-count mismatch is checked here rather than trusted from Pads, so an out-of-range cell reads 0V rather than a stale voltage.
